title: TAPER-SQRT2: tapered binary widths and precision-weighted geometric storage

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2N), the single TAPER-SQRT2 algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise r=ceil(sqrt n), m=ceil((141421/100000)r), kappa=ceil(log2m)+1, base=ceil((100759/28284200000)r), dl=base+kappa+1, H=base+m-1, L=floor(m/(4(kappa+1))), input widths base+i+min(kappa+1,floor((m-1-i)(kappa+1)/L)), exact binary/radix/high-part instrument, Kc=8192(m+10u+100), Kp=8192(u+100), u=ceil(log2n), capped extraction and full bootstrap/signed-near-parity/two-adic decoder) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8. On every execution branch total charged work O(n^(7/2)log2(n)2^((39999899241/28284200000)sqrt(n))), including every gate, bit operation, lookup, address, source cost, reset and discarded attempt. The exact growth index is1/2. These are joint uniform envelopes; logarithmic envelopes at n=1 use their positive n=2 values. Finite exhaustive copies <=N(n+10) are absorbed only through outer constants; main caps apply only on the main branch.

For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2N), the single TAPER-SQRT2 algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise r=ceil(sqrt n), m=ceil((141421/100000)r), kappa=ceil(log2m)+1, base=ceil((100759/28284200000)r), dl=base+kappa+1, H=base+m-1, L=floor(m/(4(kappa+1))), input widths base+i+min(kappa+1,floor((m-1-i)(kappa+1)/L)), exact binary/radix/high-part instrument, Kc=8192(m+10u+100), Kp=8192(u+100), u=ceil(log2n), capped extraction and full bootstrap/signed-near-parity/two-adic decoder) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8. On every execution branch peak classical workspace O(sqrt(n)2^((39999899241/28284200000)sqrt(n))) bits, with stronger main bound O(H2^H) including high fields, prefixes, radix/rank arrays, retained siblings and scratch. The exact growth index is1/2. These are joint uniform envelopes; logarithmic envelopes at n=1 use their positive n=2 values. Finite exhaustive copies <=N(n+10) are absorbed only through outer constants; main caps apply only on the main branch.

These are joint uniform envelopes; logarithmic envelopes at n=1 use their positive n=2 values. Finite exhaustive copies <=N(n+10) are absorbed only through outer constants; main caps apply only on the main branch.

For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2N), the single TAPER-SQRT2 algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise r=ceil(sqrt n), m=ceil((141421/100000)r), kappa=ceil(log2m)+1, base=ceil((100759/28284200000)r), dl=base+kappa+1, H=base+m-1, L=floor(m/(4(kappa+1))), input widths base+i+min(kappa+1,floor((m-1-i)(kappa+1)/L)), exact binary/radix/high-part instrument, Kc=8192(m+10u+100), Kp=8192(u+100), u=ceil(log2n), capped extraction and full bootstrap/signed-near-parity/two-adic decoder) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8.
